chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him).

He said: When this verse was revealed—‘And Hell is brought near on that day’ (89:23)—the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) was asked about it. He said: The Faithful Spirit informed me that Allah, there is no god but He, when He gathers together the first and the last, Hell will be brought forward, led by a thousand bridles, each bridle held by a hundred thousand harsh and severe angels. It will have a crashing sound, fury, and roaring, and it will let out a roar such that, were it not that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had postponed them to the time of reckoning, it would have destroyed the entire assembly. Then a neck will extend from it, encircling all of creation—the righteous among them and the sinners. There is not a single servant whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic created—no angel and no prophet—except that he will cry out: My Lord, save me! Save me! But you, O Prophet of Allah, will call out: My community! My community! Then a bridge will be placed over it, finer than the edge of a sword, upon which there are three arches: on the first is trustworthiness and kinship, on the second is prayer, and on the third is the justice of the Lord of the Worlds—there is no god but He. People will be required to pass over it. Kinship and trustworthiness will hold them back; if they survive that, prayer will hold them back; if they survive that, the final destination will be with the Lord of the Worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what His words, Blessed and Exalted, mean: ‘Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful’ (89:14). The people will be on the bridge—some clinging, some slipping with one foot while the other holds firm. The angels will surround them, calling out: O Forbearing One! Forgive and pardon! Return with Your bounty and grant safety! And the people will be falling into it like moths. When someone is saved by the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, he will look at it and say: Praise be to Allah who saved me from you after despair, through His grace and bounty. Indeed, our Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative (35:34).

key_terms.الأمانة: Trustworthiness; one of the three tests on the Sirat bridge
key_terms.الحساب: The reckoning; the Day of Judgment's accounting
key_terms.جهنم: Hell; the fire of the Hereafter
key_terms.شفاعة: Intercession; the Prophet's special intercession for his community
key_terms.صراط: The bridge over Hell on the Day of Judgment; thinner than a sword's edge

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the bridge over Hell and its three arches on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: The Prophet describes the terrifying scene of Hell being brought to the Day of Judgment on a thousand bridles, a neck extending from it encircling all creation, the Sirat bridge with its three arches testing trustworthiness, prayer, and divine justice, and the Prophet’s unique intercession calling out for his community while others call for themselves.
